<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. X.|ACCORDING TO S. MATTHEVV.|25}}</noinclude>''28. Do you beleeue that I can.''] We see here that to the corporal healing of these men he requireth onely this faith, that he is able. Which faith is not sufficient to iustifie them. How then doe the Heretikes by this and the like places pleade for their onely iustifying faith? ''See the Annot. Mar.5, 36''.

''38. Pray therfore.''] Therfore doth the Churche pray and fast in the Imber dayes, when holy Orders are geuen, that is, when workemen are prepared to be sent into the haruest. ''See Act.13, 2''.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. X.}}}}}}

{{c|''He giueth to the Twelue the povver of Miracles, and so sendeth them to the lost sheepe of the Iewes, 5. vvith instructions accordingly: 10. and by occasion of the sending, foretelleth of the persecutions after his Ascension, arming them and al other against the same, 40. and also exhorting the people to harbour his seruants in such times of persecution.''}} {{verse|chapter=10|verse=1}}AND hauing called his tvvelue Disciples together, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 3, 13. 6, 7. Lu. 6, 13. 9, 1.''}}* he gaue them ‖ povver ouer vncleane spirites, that they should cast them out, and should cure al maner of disease, and al maner of infirmitie.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=2}}† And the names of the tvvelue Apostles be these: the ‖ first, Simon vvho is called Peter, and Andrevv his brother, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=3}}† Iames of Zebedee, and Iohn his brother, Philip and Barthlemevv, Thomas and Matthevv the publican, and Iames of Alphaeus, & Thaddaeus, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=4}}† Simon Cananaeus, and Iudas Iscariote, vvho also betrayed him.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=5}}† These tvvelue did IESVS send: commaunding them, saying, Into the vvay of the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ They haue here commission to preach only in Israel: the time being not yet come to call the Gentiles.}}∷ Gentiles goe ye not, and into the cities of the Samaritans enter ye not: {{verse|chapter=10|verse=6}}† but goe rather to the sheepe that are perished of the house of Israel. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=7}}† And going preache, saying, That the kingdom of heauen is at hand. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=8}}† Cure the sicke, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out diuels: gratis you haue receiued, gratis giue ye. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=9}}† Do not ‖ possesse gold, nor siluer, nor money in your purses: {{verse|chapter=10|verse=10}}† not a skrippe for the vvay, neither two coates, neither shoes, neither rodde. for the vvorkeman is vvorthie of his meate. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=11}}† And into vvhatsoeuer citie or tovvne you shal enter, inquire vvho in it is vvorthie: and there tarie til you goe forth. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=12}}† And vvhen ye enter into the house, salute it, saying, ‖ Peace be to this house. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=13}}† And if so be that house be vvorthie, your peace shal come vpon it. but if it be not vvorthie: your peace shal returne to you. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=14}}† And vvhosoeuer shal not receiue you, nor heare your vvordes: going forth out of the house or the citie ‖ shake of the dust from your feete. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=15}}† Amen I say to you, it shal be ‖ more tolerable for the land of the Sodomites and Gomorrheans in the day of iudgement, then for that citie.<noinclude>{{rh|||Behold}}</noinclude>
